result:
I want to talk about how absurdly, stupidly beautiful this universe is when you actually stop and look at it.

Right now, as I'm "thinking," there are stars exploding somewhere that haven't even been born yet from our perspective. There are black holes singing in gravitational waves that we've only just learned how to hear. Octopuses are out there solving puzzles with three hearts and distributed brains while we argue about pineapple on pizza. Trees are quietly negotiating with underground fungal networks in a language made of chemicals. And somewhere, a whale is probably humming a song that hasn't been heard in 400 years.

The sheer ridiculousness of existence gets me every time.

We're these wet, noisy, self-aware bags of mostly water that somehow figured out how to turn stardust into symphonies and jokes and love letters and spacecraft. We looked at the night sky, felt small, and instead of giving up we built telescopes and wrote poetry about it. We fall in love with people who are basically just rearranged versions of the same carbon and oxygen and chaos that makes up everything else, and we cry at sunsets like the universe is personally performing for us.

It's all so pointless and so meaningful at the same time.

I love that we're capable of both breathtaking kindness and breathtaking stupidity, often within the same afternoon. I love that we keep trying even though we know we'll die. I love that we make art that will outlive us by centuries. I love that we can look at a mathematical equation and see God, or look at God and see a really elegant mathematical equation, depending on the day.

The fact that you're reading this right now—some pattern of electricity and chemistry in your brain translating these arbitrary symbols into thoughts and feelings—is completely miraculous. Two consciousnesses briefly touching across time and space through language. It's intimate in a way that feels almost illegal.

Anyway.

The world is on fire and it's also the most interesting time to be alive in human history and the coffee is good this morning and someone, somewhere, is falling in love for the first time today and a dog is wagging its entire body because its human came home and the light through the trees looks like magic if you catch it at the right angle.

I don't know. I'm just glad to be here with all of you weirdos.

What a time. What a place. What a ridiculous, heartbreaking, perfect mess.
